#77182. 21 Best Places to Visit in December in the USA

📅 31 Oct 2025 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3296 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theplanetd ↗ Open Full Page

21 Best Places to Visit in December in the USA

📅 31 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we’ll never forget the first time we visited New York City in December.
  • According to recent reports, but December travel isn’t just about snow and Santa.
  • Sources indicate that in fact, we’ve been to almost all 50 states and spent a lot of winters trying to find the most fun destinations and best weather.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we’ll never forget the first time we visited New York City in December. We’d seen it in movies, but standing there, seeing the Rockefeller Center tree all lit up for the first time, with skaters below and festive music in the air… it was pure magic.

According to recent reports, but December travel isn’t just about snow and Santa. We’ve also spent the holidays escaping to the warmth, trading snow boots for flip-flops.

Sources indicate that in fact, we’ve been to almost all 50 states and spent a lot of winters trying to find the most fun destinations and best weather. We’ve done so many road trips in the USA and flown almost everywhere, trying to find the best places to either escape the snow or enjoy the winter, you would think we are obsessed. And we want to share all of that knowledge with you.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking for the perfect winter getaway, you have a clear choice: either lean into the winter magic or escape it completely. Are you dreaming of a warm-weather escape with sunshine and sand, or a storybook Christmas town that looks like a real-life snow globe?

Based on all those experiences, we’ve put together this list of our favourite places to visit. Whether you’re looking for a festive city, a snowy mountain, or a sunny beach, we’ll help you find the perfect spot.

Here is a quick look at some of the best places for a December getaway in the USA, from festive winter wonderlands to sunny escapes.

December is a month of pure magic and festive energy. It’s the perfect time to use up that last bit of vacation time for the year. The biggest draw is the distinct choice it offers: You can either dive head-first into a winter wonderland, complete with snow and holiday markets, or you can completely escape the cold weather and find yourself on a sunny beach. It’s a month of festive celebrations, incredible decorations, and finding the perfect atmosphere to end the year.

In a recent development, if you’re anything like us, sometimes the best gift in December is a break from the cold. Trust us, we know after living in Toronto, Canada. Those winters are brutal. These are our favourite spots to find sunshine and warm weather, where you can trade your winter coat for a light jacket or even a swimsuit.

We love the laid-back, quirky vibe of Key West, and it’s even more special in December. We have a great memory of biking around the island, seeing the historic inns draped in holiday lights, and then ending the day at Mallory Square for the sunset celebration. It’s a perfect escape from the cold.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: This is the perfect time to visit. The summer humidity is gone, the weather is sunny and warm (often in the high 70s), and the risk of hurricanes is very low. The whole island is in a festive spirit, with unique events like the “Bight Before Christmas” boat parade.

Where to Stay: We recommend finding a guesthouse or inn in the historic Old Town to be close to the action.

We once went to a holiday luau in Ka’anapali, and it’s an experience we’ll never forget. You’re eating kalua pork and sipping a mai tai, watching a beautiful hula performance… and then Santa Claus arrives on an outrigger canoe. It was the perfect, uniquely Hawaiian way to get into the festive spirit.

In a recent development, why Visit in December: You get tropical weather, festive holiday luaus, and it’s the official start of the humpback whale watching season. Be aware that this is a popular time, especially around Christmas, so prices can be high and you’ll need to book in advance.

Where to Stay: Look to the resorts in Wailea or Ka’anapali for a classic Maui experience.

We’ll always remember snorkeling the underwater trail at Trunk Bay in St. John. The water was so calm and clear, and seeing all the colourful fish felt a world away from the snow back home. That’s the magic of a Caribbean trip in December, and the USVI makes it so easy for American travelers.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: It’s the start of the dry season, with fantastic weather and warm, clear water. You get a full-on tropical, warm-weather Christmas experience, all without needing a passport.

Sources indicate that where to Stay: You can choose from large resorts in St. Thomas or more eco-friendly villas and lodges in St. John.

Recent findings suggest that we were not prepared for how magical St. Augustine is in December. We took one of the Old Town trolley tours at night, and seeing the entire historic city, from the old Spanish architecture to the palm trees, draped in millions of white lights… it was breathtaking. It’s a holiday light display unlike any other.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: The famous “Nights of Lights” festival. The entire city is illuminated, and the mild Florida weather is perfect for walking around and enjoying the atmosphere. It’s one of the most festive and warm places you can visit.

Where to Stay: We recommend a historic inn or bed & breakfast in the downtown district to be within walking distance of all the lights.

It has been revealed that while Maui is our go-to for a resort escape, Honolulu is where you go for a vibrant, city-meets-beach holiday. We loved seeing the massive Santa surfing with his reindeer in the fountain at the Iolani Palace. The whole city has this amazing “Mele Kalikimaka” (Merry Christmas) spirit.

Why Visit in December: It’s the perfect blend of warm beach weather, world-class shopping, and festive displays. It’s also a significant month for history, with the memorial events at Pearl Harbor.

Where to Stay: Waikiki has a huge range of hotels, from historic beachfront properties to modern high-rises.

According to recent reports, if your idea of a winter getaway is to truly get away from everything, the crowds, the noise, the stress, then South Padre is a perfect choice. We spent a week there, and our days consisted of long, quiet walks on the beach. It was a total reset and the perfect way to escape the winter blues.

Recent findings suggest that why Visit in December: The weather is mild, and the crowds are gone. It’s one of the warmest places in Texas and offers a simple, relaxing beach vacation without the high prices or holiday chaos of other destinations.

Where to Stay: You’ll find many beachfront condos and hotels offering great off-season rates.

It has been revealed that we thought we knew desert holiday lights, but the “Las Noches de las Luminarias” at the Desert Botanical Garden in Phoenix is on another level. Walking the garden paths lit by thousands of hand-lit luminaria bags, with musicians playing, was a top-tier holiday experience.

Why Visit in December: You get two trips in one: perfect, sunny weather for outdoor adventures like hiking during the day, and stunning, sophisticated holiday light displays at night.

Where to Stay: Choose from upscale resorts in Scottsdale or stylish hotels in downtown Phoenix.

Sources indicate that sometimes, the warm weather destinations just won’t cut it, especially if you are looking for that winter wonderland feel. So, this section is for travellers who want to dive head-first into the holiday spirit. These are the cities and towns that go all-out for December, with millions of lights, Christmas markets, and an atmosphere of pure magic.

We’ve visited NYC many times, but there’s a specific energy in December. We grabbed hot chocolates and walked through the Bryant Park Winter Village, watching the ice skaters zip around the rink under the lights of the surrounding skyscrapers. It felt like being in the opening scene of a holiday movie. There is nothing like Latest York City at Christmas.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: It is the quintessential American Christmas destination. From the iconic tree to the world-famous window displays, the entire city is on a different level of festive.

Where to Stay: Midtown is convenient for seeing the main holiday sights, but we also love the West Village for its cosy, neighbourhood feel.

Industry observers note that we’d heard Leavenworth was a “Christmas Town,” but we weren’t prepared for the reality. We visited during the Village of Lights festival, and walking through the snow-covered Bavarian-style village while every single building was covered in over half a million lights… it’s not an exaggeration. It’s the closest we’ve ever felt to being inside a real-life snow globe.

Why Visit in December: The entire town transforms into a “Hallmark movie” Christmas village. It’s a full-immersion holiday experience with carolers, festive food, and incredible decorations.

Where to Stay: Book a Bavarian-style lodge or inn right in the village. You must book many months in advance for December.

Sources indicate that we love Asheville, but visiting in December is all about the Biltmore Estate. We took the candlelight evening tour, and seeing the main banquet hall with its 35-foot tree, fireplaces roaring, and carolers singing… it felt like we’d stepped back in time into a Gilded Age Christmas party.

Recent findings suggest that why Visit in December: Christmas at Biltmore is one of the most iconic holiday events in the country. The city itself is a cosy mountain retreat, and the Blue Ridge Mountains are just beautiful with a dusting of snow.

Where to Stay: You can stay on the Biltmore Estate for the full experience or choose a boutique hotel downtown.

Here are the remaining destinations for the “Best Christmas Towns & Festive Cities” section, all written with unique, December-focused content.

In a recent development, we’ve visited a lot of Christmas markets, but visiting the one in Bethlehem, known as “Christmas City USA”, just felt right. We sipped hot cider and browsed the stalls in the old quarter, and you can feel the city’s 250+ years of Christmas tradition. The whole place is lit by the glow of a giant Moravian star on the hillside.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: This is Christmas City USA. It was nicknamed this on Christmas Eve, 1741. It offers one of the most authentic and historic holiday experiences in the country, blending its Moravian heritage with a European-style Christkindlmarkt.

Where to Stay: Look for a hotel or inn in the historic downtown area to be close to the festivities.

Industry observers note that walking into Solvang in December felt like we’d been transported to a Danish village during its Julefest celebration. We spent the day exploring the half-timbered buildings, windmills, and bakeries, all decorated for the holidays. It’s such a unique and charming way to experience a winter getaway in the middle of California.

Why Visit in December: The town’s month-long “Julefest” (Yule-fest) celebration is in full swing. It’s a one-of-a-kind Danish-style Christmas with parades, markets, and, of course, delicious European pastries.

Where to Stay: Choose one of the charming Danish-themed inns right in the village to be in the middle of the Julefest activities.

Industry observers note that we had to see the “Christmas Capital of Texas” for ourselves, and it did not disappoint. The entire historic Main Street is transformed. We loved seeing the vintage railroad, which becomes the “North Pole Express” for the month. They take the “Christmas Capital” title seriously; there are over 1,400 events in 40 days.

Why Visit in December: It is the officially designated “Christmas Capital of Texas”. The sheer number of festive events, light displays, and activities is staggering, making it a top-tier destination for families and holiday lovers.

Where to Stay: The Gaylord Texan Resort is an attraction in itself, or you can stay near the Historic Main Street to be close to the events.

Recent findings suggest that A New Orleans Christmas is an experience all its own. We did a “Reveillon Dinner,” a modern take on a Creole holiday tradition, and it was one of the most memorable meals we’ve ever had. Afterwards, we walked to Jackson Square to see the St. Louis Cathedral all lit up while carolers sang.

Why Visit in December: You get to experience unique Creole Christmas traditions you won’t find anywhere else. The weather is mild, the food is incredible, and the city’s lobbies (like at The Roosevelt) have some of the most elegant decorations we’ve seen.

Where to Stay: We recommend a hotel in the French Quarter to be in the middle of the action and see the decorated lobbies.

We went to Natchitoches (pronounced Nak-a-tish) specifically for its Christmas Festival, and it was a total joy. It’s one of the oldest and biggest in the country. The whole city, which is the oldest in Louisiana, lights up with over 300,000 lights along the Cane River, and the weekly fireworks shows are fantastic.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: It hosts one of the oldest and most celebrated holiday festivals in the US, running for six weeks. It’s a classic, Southern Christmas experience in a beautiful historic district.

Where to Stay: Book a room at a historic bed & breakfast in the downtown area.

Visiting Colonial Williamsburg in December felt like walking through a living history Christmas card. We joined a candlelight tour, and seeing the historic buildings lit by real candles in the windows, with carolers in period costumes and the smell of woodsmoke in the air… it was absolutely magical.

Why Visit in December: You get to experience a traditional, 18th-century “Colonial Christmas”. The decorations are all-natural (no plastic lights), and the atmosphere is incredibly authentic and charming.

Where to Stay: Stay in one of the historic Colonial Houses or a tavern right in the restored area for the full immersive experience.

Here is the final category of destinations. This section is all about embracing the snow and finding that perfect winter wonderland.

Industry observers note that for many, holiday season travel is all about finding that perfect, snowy scene. These are the places to go for world-class skiing, cosy lodges, and that magical feeling of a true winter escape.

We’ll always remember our first “après-ski” in Aspen. We had spent the day on the mountain hitting fresh powder whenever we got the chance, and as the sun went down, the sky lit up with this incredible pink and orange light they call “Aspenglow.” Sitting by a fire, enjoying a glass of Christmas cheer, and watching the snow fall on the historic town, it just felt like the peak of a luxury winter trip.

Why Visit in December: It’s one of the world’s most famous upscale ski destinations, and the town is just as much an attraction as the mountains. The festive atmosphere, high-end shops, and restaurants are all decked out for the holidays.

Where to Stay: Aspen is known for its luxury hotels and ski-in/ski-out resorts.

In a recent development, one of our favourite things about Park City is its history. We loved skiing down to the historic Main Street, popping off our skis, and walking straight into a saloon that’s been there since the silver mining days. It feels like a real Western town, not just a ski resort.

Why Visit in December: It’s a historic mountain town with two world-class ski resorts (Park City and Deer Valley). The historic Main Street is incredibly charming, and the “Snow Globe Stroll” features life-sized snow globes you can walk through.

Where to Stay: You can find ski-in/ski-out hotels or stay at an inn on the historic Main Street.

Jackson Hole in December is just dramatic. We took a sleigh ride through the National Elk Refuge, and seeing thousands of elk gathered against the backdrop of the snow-covered Teton mountains… it was a powerful and wild winter experience we’ve never forgotten.

Why Visit in December: It’s the perfect mix of rugged “cowboy Christmas” charm and some of the most challenging ski terrain in North America. The town square, with its famous antler arches, is beautifully lit for the holidays.

Where to Stay: Stay at a slopeside resort in Teton Village or in a hotel in the town of Jackson.

According to recent reports, we love Whitefish because it feels like a real, down-to-earth ski town. We spent a day snowshoeing in nearby Glacier National Park, enjoying the total silence and incredible snowy landscapes, and then came back to town for a casual dinner. It’s all the beauty, without the glitz. Just what we were looking for in a winter vacation.

It has been revealed that why Visit in December: It’s a laid-back, charming mountain town with a top-rated ski resort and stunning scenery. It’s also right next to Glacier National Park, which is a spectacular place to explore in the winter.

Where to Stay: You can find lodges on the mountain or stay in one of the friendly inns in downtown Whitefish.

This was a trip purely for the fun of it, and it was 100% worth it. You drive down streets named “Santa Claus Lane” and “St. Nicholas Drive,” the streetlights are shaped like candy canes, and you can visit the Santa Claus House and see his reindeer. It’s a surreal and joyful experience.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: It’s the ultimate Christmas fantasy come to life. The entire town is Christmas-themed, 365 days a year, but it’s most magical in December with real snow on the ground and the added bonus of possibly seeing the Northern Lights.

Where to Stay: North Pole is very small; most visitors stay in the nearby city of Fairbanks, which has a wide range of hotels.

For the best warm weather, your top choices are Southern Florida (like Key West), Hawaii (like Maui and Honolulu), and the desert Southwest (like Phoenix and Palm Springs). The U.S. Virgin Islands are also a fantastic passport-free tropical option.

In a recent development, leavenworth, Washington, is often considered the ultimate “Christmas town” as it looks just like a Bavarian snow globe. Other top choices include Bethlehem, PA (known as “Christmas City USA”), Solvang, CA (for a Danish-style Julefest), and Grapevine, TX (the “Christmas Capital of Texas”).

Sources indicate that yes, but it depends on the park. It’s the perfect time to visit desert parks like Death Valley, Everglades, and Significant Bend, where summer heat is unbearable. However, many mountain parks like Glacier, Yellowstone, and parts of Yosemite are mostly inaccessible due to heavy snow and road closures.

You are almost guaranteed to find snow in the mountain towns of the Rockies, like Aspen, CO, Park City, UT, and Jackson Hole, WY. You’ll also find snow in the Cascade Mountains (like Leavenworth, WA), Alaska, and the mountains around Lake Tahoe.

December is a magical month to travel. Whether you’re chasing the sun, seeking out that perfect snowy scene, or looking for a town that’s full of holiday magic, the US has the perfect spot for you.

We hope this list, based on our own winter travels, helps you plan your next getaway. Save this on Pinterest for your holiday planning! Where is your favourite place to go in December?

At Dior’s First Spa in Venice, Old Glamour Gets the Hi-Tech Treatment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the buzz of the Venice Film Festival has only just died down, when I step out of a Riva boat that bobs at the berth of the Hotel Cipriani Venice on Giudecca Island.
  • Venice’s links with Dior go back to 1951 when the French couture brand’s eponymous founder fell in love with the city after attending the Ball of the Century costume party at the Palazzo Labia, hosted by art collector Charles de Beistegui.
  • Sources indicate that sophia Loren and Julia Roberts are just a few of the starry names to have stayed at this classic hotel, which launched its new spa in July 2026 as part of ongoing renovations led by New York architect Peter Marino.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the buzz of the Venice Film Festival has only just died down, when I step out of a Riva boat that bobs at the berth of the Hotel Cipriani Venice on Giudecca Island. I’m excited but also exhausted after spending the previous ten days on several long-haul flights, and I fear it’s beginning to affect my conversational skills—and my collagen levels. Luckily, I’m not here to attend a premiere or hop between Biennale events. I'm here to experience Cipriani's newly opened Dior Spa, the fashion house's first in Venice.

Venice’s links with Dior go back to 1951 when the French couture brand’s eponymous founder fell in love with the city after attending the Ball of the Century costume party at the Palazzo Labia, hosted by art collector Charles de Beistegui.

The views from my suite's private terrace.

A welcome Dior takeover on Cip's ground floor.

Sources indicate that sophia Loren and Julia Roberts are just a few of the starry names to have stayed at this classic hotel, which launched its new spa in July 2026 as part of ongoing renovations led by New York architect Peter Marino. The cream and pastel palette channels an 18th-century Venetian Rococo spirit, with elegant mid-century Italian stucco and terrazzo flooring. Science-driven skincare nerds tend to believe that fashion houses can’t run beauty departments worthy of their approval, but Dior has the potential to persuade them otherwise. Many luxury spas are often either visually stunning temples that offer underwhelming treatments, or medically-driven centers that leave you glowing but feeling as if you’re in a hospital. Dior combines the best of both worlds, recalling an old-school glamour while deploying higher-tech treatments that aren’t geared towards “maxxing” but aim for clients to look and feel their best in a tranquil environment.

The Dior Spa's La Collection Privée island.

One of the Dior Spa's Murano chandeliers.

Sources indicate that after spending the morning in Murano watching the world’s most talented glassblowers at work, I head down to the spa’s marbled entrance where a Murano chandelier dangles above a centerpiece table festooned with beautiful bottles of parfums from Dior’s La Collection Privée, including Tobacolore and, my favorite fragrance, La Colle Noire. I’m handed a rose infusion before slipping into cloud-soft Dior slippers and waiting outside my treatment room for one of the signature treatments, which include Le Théâtre Corporal, a four-handed, Ayurvedic-inspired massage (which couples can do together), and the Golden Aura hydrafacial. But I’m here for what feels like the most apt option in a city famed for its masked balls: the Mascarade facial.

Setting up for a canalside Dior masterclass.

Industry observers note that developed by the brand’s global skincare ambassador, Hadda Akrim, the Mascarade aims to regenerate the skin and soothe the mind. I’m in need of it now that my circadian rhythm is disrupted after back-to-back flights, cabin pressure and changing time zones. The treatment is more than just a facial: it involves 90 minutes of drainage, rebalancing, and re-boosting with the help of devices that encourage the nutrients being massaged into your skin to sink deeper. Firstly, I lie on the treatment table to receive an abdominal massage, which rebalances my nervous system (the gut is our second brain, after all) and restores my inner harmony to maximize my radiance.

Industry observers note that next, ultrasound waves are applied across my face to improve the skin’s elasticity and circulation, followed by microcurrent muscle stimulation during which I literally feel my cells awakening. The procedure soothes my mind so much I fall into a contented sleep. It’s all designed to boost my complexion’s glow—and it works. Dior’s global spa director, Olivier Hahn, told me he’s most proud of the sonic component of the spa offering, which does its job by calming me down without me even noticing.

A heavenly breakfast in my top-floor suite.

The best kind of antioxidants at Oro restaurant.

I wake up for the next stage of the treatment, a technical jaw massage, which the facialist carries out to counteract my nighttime teeth-grinding. She then places cryogenic stones over a cooling mask to firm, drain, and reoxygenate my skin. It’s a perfect way to re-enter the world, cognitively and physically. I feel snatched as I sip coffee by the pool after the treatment. The Mascarade facial is great for a morning-after depuffing, but, given the OMGs I receive from fellow spa-goers, I conclude that it’s also perfect for an evening out. I head out into the Venetian night with nothing but a touch of mascara and a post-facial luminosity.

Feeling like a kid on Christmas morning, the staff sent me on my way with a bag of the Dior Prestige products to keep up my skincare routine back home. The ingredients are mainly organic, something I hadn’t expected. In the same way that historic French vineyards downplay their organic practices for fear of alienating clients disdainful of natural wines, Dior also keeps its products' natural roots on the down low. It all comes as a pleasant surprise and further cements this spa’s authority in the world of regenerative beauty therapy.

A version of this story originally appeared in Condé Nast Traveller UK.

MarineXchange (MXP) has appointed Philipp Grasmug as its chief technology officer (CTO).

In this role, he will lead MXP’s technology strategy, product engineering and the continued development of the MXP Enterprise Platform, with a strong focus on security, scalability and AI.

Michael Eder, CEO of MXP, welcomed Grasmug to MXP, commenting: “As the leading software partner for the cruise industry, we attract top technology talent and leaders. Philipp’s experience in building and scaling business-critical software comes at exactly the right time as we take the next step in our growth story.”.

With more than 20 years of experience in developing complex software products for essential business operations, Grasmug most recently served as CTO of UBIMET Group, where he led 30 engineers and a global weather forecasting platform used by clients in insurance, critical infrastructure and renewable energy.

He brings deep expertise in scalable platforms, data-driven product development, AI and building high-performing engineering teams and he co-founded Reactive Reality, taking virtual try-on technology from concept to market.

In a recent development, “I am excited to join MXP and its talented team. The MXP Enterprise Platform already powers operations for more than 60 cruise brands, and that gives us a unique foundation to build on,” stated Grasmug.

“My focus will be on streamlining and scaling our platform, bringing AI and agentic features into our products in ways that create real value, and making sure our customers can rely on technology that is secure, modern and ready for the future of cruising.”.

This follows the recent announcement of a definitive agreement MXP signed with Deep Wave Maritime Technologies Group.

Under the deal, MXP will broaden the services available to its customers as part of Deep Wave, while continuing to operate under its own brand.

Massie moves to force Hegseth impeachment vote

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday.
  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the matter could occur by Wednesday.
  • A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the matter could occur by Wednesday.

A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Massie's resolution also charges Hegseth with disregarding protection of civilians in wartime and suppressing the free speech of a U.S. senator.

Massie confirmed his intention to file the resolution as a matter of the privileges of the House.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., will now have to rule as to whether the resolution constitutes a proper question of the privileges of the House. There is precedent from prior instances when impeachment was found to be valid as it relates to the House’s constitutionally granted powers.

In a recent development, he must schedule a vote to occur within two legislative days. Assuming that the speaker rules that Massie's resolution is privileged, the House could vote on the resolution itself, or on a motion to table it or refer it to committee.

Sources indicate that if the House were to impeach Hegseth under this process, it would mark a historical anomaly. According to the Congressional Research Service, recent attempts to impeach an official as a matter of the privileges of the House have not resulted in approval of the resolution. In cases in which an official has been impeached, the House has nearly always chosen to conduct an investigation first.

It has been revealed that in an interview on Oct. 26, Massie put the chances of his resolution being adopted at 50-50.

In comments to reporters outside the Capitol after his floor remarks, Massie stated he suspected some Republicans may back his resolution but he indicated he has neither asked for nor received any such assurances from any of them.

In a recent development, he predicted there could be some GOP support in the Senate if Hegseth is impeached and it goes to trial. He noted that if the trial does not start until 2027, any Republicans who might vote to convict Hegseth would presumably be joined by most if not all of a more sizeable Senate Democratic caucus.

Massie's odds of success for his resolution may now be greater than his previous 50-50 prediction given the results of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which gave Democrats control over both chambers in the next Congress — a vote motivated largely by opposition to the Iran war and its inflationary impact.

Sources indicate that the questions now are, first, how many House Republicans will defy President Donald Trump and vote to impeach Hegseth; and, secondly, how many incumbents who lost their reelection bids on Nov. 3, a cohort that is disproportionately Republican, might be absent for the impeachment vote?

Massie mentioned some Republicans who lost their reelection bids may feel freer to vote to impeach Hegseth. And he also said Republicans who were reelected and will have to face voters in 2028 may also think about how their vote on an impeachment resolution would reverberate politically.

It has been revealed that "It's going to be everybody's conscience, and then they'll have to live with that vote," Massie noted. "And they're going to have to live with that vote two years from now if they're not part of the retirement caucus. And if they were part of the retirement caucus, what do they have to lose?".

Asked why he did not bring articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump, Massie noted: "I think the president needs to see one of — this is a metaphor — one of his horses shot out from under him, and then maybe he'll he will see things differently.".

If the House does vote on Massie’s resolution, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is expected to become the House speaker in the next Congress, said on ABC’s “This Week” on Sunday that he would be a “hard yes” on it.

Sources indicate that hegseth has “got to go,” Jeffries said. “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe.”.

Most if not all House Democrats are expected to agree.

Last week, Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., the ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and its likely chairman in the next Congress, indicated in an interview with The Newly introduced Republic that he would support Massie’s impeachment resolution, and he predicted it would be adopted.

It has been revealed that referring to Massie’s measure, Smith said, “By every estimation, it will pass and he will be impeached. And off that goes to the Senate. Then the Senate is legally required to spend all of their time dealing with that until it’s done with.”.

"Every second Pete Hegseth remains at the top of the Pentagon, our servicemembers are at risk," Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., a senior member of the Armed Services Committee, remarked in a post on X on Sunday.

Also on Monday, Everett B. Kelley, the national president of the American Federation of Government Employees, a union that represents some 820,000 federal and D.C. government employees, sent a letter to House members urging a “yes” vote on Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution.

The letter cited the risks Kelley remarked the Iran war has posed to the lives of the Defense Department's uniformed and civilian personnel, and the missive noted Hegseth's stripping of workplace rights and protections for the department's civilians.

"By adopting Rep. Massie’s resolution, the House can begin the long overdue bipartisan effort to reclaim its constitutional powers and authority, restore checks and balances, and take responsibility for the lives of military personnel and civilian employees that Mr. Hegseth’s capricious leadership has jeopardized," Kelley wrote.

Massie announced in mid-September his intention to file an impeachment resolution against Hegseth. But Johnson adjourned the House before the vote would have occurred.

Massie’s fresh resolution is substantially the same as his earlier one, with the same eight articles of impeachment.

The first three of these alleges that Hegseth’s conduct of the Iran war violated the War Powers Resolution.

Massie's measure claims Hegseth prosecuted the Iran war without congressional authorization and in the absence of an attack on the United States or an imminent threat.

Industry observers note that further, the measure alleges that Hegseth continued the war despite the House and Senate adopting in June a concurrent war powers resolution calling for the withdrawal of U.S. forces from the fight.

And, the resolution states, Hegseth continued the Iran war after the expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period.

Massie’s measure further asserts that Hegseth:.

According to recent reports, the House has only voted twice to impeach a member of the Cabinet. In 1876, Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached over allegations of corruption, and his abrupt resignation likely contributed to his acquittal in the Senate.

In 2024, the House voted 214-213 to impeach Alejandro Mayorkas, then-secretary of Homeland Security, for “willful and systemic refusal to comply with the law” and “breach of public trust.” The Senate dispensed with the charges without a trial.

Both join Ambassador on January 4, 2027, from JTA Travel Group, taking up their new positions within the trade team led by Nicola Harper, Ambassador’s head of distribution.

“With Ambassador continuing to expand its offering both in the UK and across Europe, we remain fully committed to working closely with our trade partners and ensuring they have everything they need to succeed,” commented Harper.

Sources indicate that “With this in mind, I’m delighted to welcome Louise and Chris to the Ambassador family. In her fresh role as national commercial manager, Winter will support Ambassador’s national trade relationships, identify new business opportunities and help drive sales growth across the UK.

She brings more than 25 years’ experience across the travel and retail sectors, most recently as group head of operations at JTA Travel Group, where she has overseen commercial and operational performance across JTA Travel since February 2024.

Sources indicate that “I’m thrilled to be joining Ambassador Cruise Line at such an exciting time for the business. Ambassador has a fantastic proposition, strong ambitions for growth and, importantly, a real commitment to the travel trade – something I’m extremely passionate about,” mentioned Winter.

As divisional sales manager – North, Cundall will be responsible for developing existing commercial relationships across the North of England, Scotland and Northern Ireland to maximize sales opportunities and drive day-to-day trading, while identifying fresh agent and trade partnerships.

He joins Ambassador from JTA Travel Group, where he oversees sales strategy and commercial relationships across the UK travel trade.

“I’m absolutely delighted to be joining Ambassador Cruise Line as Divisional Sales Manager North. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

North Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for latest member orientation. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

But as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep. Tim Moore, the influential former speaker of the North Carolina House and a chief architect of the gerrymander that aimed to keep the 14th District safely red.

David Rouzer led Democratic social worker Kimberly Hardy by less than a point.

The Democratic rout in the midterm elections was powered by victories in states with upcoming GOP-favored maps, including Texas, Ohio and Florida.

Sources indicate that the repeated rounds of redistricting may have also erased some of the advantages of incumbency, according to Peter L. And I think that that came back and hurt Republicans in this cycle.”.

Doug Heye, a GOP strategist and a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee, said redistricting “ticked off a whole lot of voters, and really activated the Democratic base.”.

Republican incumbents accustomed to winning by comfortable margins weren’t prepared for a political environment driven by anger over the war in Iran and angst about the rising cost of living.

Recent findings suggest that “Clearly, a lot of those Republicans didn’t take their elections seriously,” Heye noted. “They won last time with 18 points. They weren't on anyone's radar screen, so they didn't think they had to do anything.”.

Womack credits her win to a grassroots campaign centered on economic problems. While her race wasn’t on the national radar – Moore, after all, won by 16 points in 2024 – and her campaign didn’t have money for ads, she was out in the district doing events every day.

“There are a lot of working families right now who are in the missing middle,” she said in an interview. “They make too much money to get help, but they don't make enough money to get ahead. … Someone who can be working a full-time job, but still doesn’t have enough money to buy groceries or to afford their medications or to have access to health insurance.”.

Sources indicate that “There are so many people who [understand] what happens when you're down on your luck and you don't have enough money to make good financial decisions,’’ she remarked. “Most people don't want those bad decisions to be a definition of their character for the rest of their life.”.

Early in the midterm cycle, Democratic opposition research group American Bridge prepared detailed dossiers on Republican House incumbents in North Carolina.

Airport Luggage Tag Scam: How to Protect Your Checked Bags in 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine walking up to customs after a long international flight and being told that a suitcase connected to your name has been flagged.
  • Then the officer points to the luggage tag and says, “Then why is your name on it?”.
  • That is the nightmare behind a luggage scam travelers need to understand in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine walking up to customs after a long international flight and being told that a suitcase connected to your name has been flagged.

Then the officer points to the luggage tag and says, “Then why is your name on it?”.

That is the nightmare behind a luggage scam travelers need to understand in 2026. It is called baggage tag switching, and it is exactly what it sounds like: the luggage tag from an innocent passenger’s checked suitcase is allegedly removed and placed onto another bag.

Sources indicate that baggage tag switching scams happen when the luggage tag from a traveler’s checked bag is allegedly removed and placed on another suitcase. To protect yourself, take a video of your suitcase before check-in, photograph the bag on the scale, take a close-up photo of the baggage tag, keep your baggage receipt, place a tracker inside your suitcase, and report any damaged, missing, delayed, or retagged bag before leaving the airport.

According to a W5 investigation, innocent passengers flying from Canada have been detained after their real luggage tags were allegedly moved onto suitcases containing illegal drugs. The investigation focused on flights from Canada and alleged cases connected to Toronto Pearson, but the larger lesson applies to travelers everywhere: once your checked bag disappears behind the counter, you are trusting the system to protect your luggage, your tag, and your name.

We have traveled to more than 130 countries on all seven continents, and checked bags have always been part of travel. But the old habit of simply handing over your suitcase and hoping for the best needs an update.

Industry observers note that in 2026, protecting your checked luggage is not just about stopping theft. It is about protecting the paper trail that connects you to your bag.

This is part of a bigger shift in how travelers need to think about airport safety, baggage scams, and common airport security mistakes before they fly.

Editor’s note: This article is based on our video about baggage tag switching, which has reached more than 86,000 views on our travel YouTube channel.

Before you check a bag, take two minutes to create proof that the bag is yours.

It also helps to run through a full pre-travel checklist before you leave for the airport so you are not rushing through check-in.

Recent findings suggest that this may sound like a lot, but it takes less than two minutes at check-in. And those two minutes could matter if your name ever gets attached to a suitcase that is not yours.

We covered this luggage tag scam in detail in the video below, including the simple two-minute routine we now recommend before checking a bag.

Baggage tag switching is when the tag printed for your checked luggage is removed from your actual suitcase and attached to another bag.

In a recent development, when you check luggage, the airline prints a baggage tag that usually includes your name, flight, destination, routing information, barcode, and bag number. That tag is the airport system’s way of connecting that suitcase to you.

The problem is that once your bag goes behind the counter, you cannot see what happens next.

It has been revealed that in the alleged scheme reported by W5, corrupt baggage or ramp workers could remove a legitimate tag from a passenger’s suitcase and attach it to another suitcase heading to the same destination. If that second bag is intercepted, the paperwork points back to the innocent passenger.

It has been revealed that that is what makes this scam so dangerous. You may have done everything right: checked your own suitcase, kept your boarding pass, and boarded your flight. But behind the scenes, one strip of paper may now connect your name to a bag you have never seen.

Most airport workers are honest. Let’s be clear about that. The vast majority are doing hard jobs under pressure, moving thousands of bags through complex systems every day. But a baggage system only needs a few bad actors to create a very serious problem.

This story has received attention because of Canadian cases, but this is not only a Canada problem.

The bigger issue is that every major airport has the same basic weak point: you hand over your suitcase, it enters a restricted area, and from that point on, you are relying on the system to protect the tag, the bag, and the records connected to your name.

Sources indicate that that is true in Toronto. It is true in Latest York, London, Paris, Dubai, Bangkok, Mexico City, Sydney, and anywhere else checked luggage moves behind the scenes.

International travel also adds another layer of risk. If your name gets tied to a suspicious bag in another country, you may be dealing with a different legal system, different customs procedures, and possibly a language barrier.

In a recent development, the Government of Canada warns travelers that drug offences abroad can have serious consequences and that you should never carry anything across a border for someone else. The Canada Border Services Agency also specifically reminds travelers that trafficking cannabis or other drugs across the border is a criminal offence and warns people to beware of anyone asking them to carry something.

That is why documenting your own luggage matters. You are not being paranoid. You are creating a simple evidence trail.

Before your suitcase disappears behind the counter, take a clear video of it.

In a recent development, do a full 360-degree view. Show the front, back, sides, wheels, handles, color, brand, straps, stickers, scratches, dents, or anything that makes your bag identifiable.

Yes, you may feel ridiculous filming your suitcase at the airport. Do it anyway. People film lattes. You can film the thing that might keep you out of a holding room.

This video creates a time-stamped record of what your suitcase looked like before it left your hands. If someone later claims a different bag is yours, you have proof of what your actual luggage looked like at check-in.

When your bag is placed on the airline scale, take a quick photo or video showing the weight.

According to recent reports, this matters because weight is part of the paper trail. If your suitcase weighed 19 kilograms at check-in and another suitcase connected to your name weighs 32 kilograms, that difference may matter.

You are not trying to become a detective. You are simply creating a record that states this was your bag, this was the weight, this was the condition, and this was the tag attached to it.

That is the kind of simple documentation that can help if your bag is delayed, damaged, retagged, or questioned later.

Once the airline attaches the baggage tag to your suitcase, take a close-up photo or video of it before the bag goes onto the conveyor belt.

Make sure you can clearly see the barcode, destination airport, flight number, routing, and bag number. Also check that the airline has looped and attached the tag properly.

You are not being difficult. You are checking the one strip of paper connecting you to your luggage. That little tag is doing a lot of legal heavy lifting.

Air Canada’s own baggage information explains that self-service kiosks can print baggage tags, receipts, and boarding passes, and that travelers then attach the tags and proceed to bag drop. That means passengers are often handling or reviewing this paperwork themselves before the bag disappears into the system.

Never throw away the little baggage receipt sticker you receive at check-in.

It has been revealed that keep it somewhere safe. Don’t stuff it in a random pocket, lose it before boarding, or assume the airline app is enough. Put it with your passport or travel documents until your suitcase is back in your hands.

Sources indicate that that receipt usually contains your bag number. If something goes wrong, that number becomes part of the evidence trail. That number can help airline staff or investigators compare what you checked, what arrived, and whether someone intercepted or retagged another bag.

This is one of the easiest travel habits to fix, and it costs nothing.

Before you close your checked bag, take one clear photo of the inside.

Industry observers note that you do not need to photograph every sock like you are filing a museum inventory. Just take one clear photo of the contents: clothes, shoes, toiletries, chargers, jackets, and the usual chaos of travel.

This helps show what you actually packed. If a suitcase connected to your name contains items you have never seen, you have a record of what was inside your real bag before check-in.

This is especially useful on international trips, where proving what you packed may become more complicated once you are outside your home country.

It is also a good reminder to double-check what not to pack in checked luggage before you leave for the airport.

A luggage tracker will not stop someone from tampering with a baggage tag, but it can help show where your real suitcase went.

We use Apple AirTags, but there are also Tile trackers, Samsung SmartTags, and other luggage tracking options.

The notable thing is this: put the tracker inside your suitcase. Do not hang it outside where it can easily be removed.

If authorities are asking about a suitcase connected to your name and your tracker reveals your actual suitcase is somewhere else, that becomes another part of your evidence trail.

Trackers are also helpful if your bag arrives late, gets separated from its original tag, or ends up in the wrong baggage area. They are not perfect, but they give travelers one more layer of information when airline systems fail.

We use AirTags in our checked bags, but Samsung SmartTags and Tile trackers are also good options depending on your phone. The key is to keep the tracker inside the suitcase where it cannot easily be removed.

We also recommend pairing a luggage tracker with a few simple anti-theft travel accessories especially on longer international trips.

A plain black suitcase is basically the airport version of camouflage.

Sources indicate that make your luggage easier to identify with a bright strap, ribbon, sticker, or distinctive luggage tag. You want to be able to spot your bag quickly and prove what makes it different from hundreds of others.

Recent findings suggest that but do not put too much personal information on the outside. Your name and phone number are enough.

You do not need your home address waving around the baggage hall like an invitation that says, “Please rob us while we’re in Italy.”.

Keep luggage identifiable, but not overly revealing.

This rule has always mattered, but it matters even more now.

Never carry a package, gift, suitcase, envelope, or item for someone else. That means no favors for strangers, no “harmless” packages, and no quick airport errands for someone you barely know.

If you did not pack it, you do not carry it.

The CBSA specifically warns travelers to beware of people who ask them to carry anything and notes that consequences for drug trafficking can be serious in Canada and abroad.

That is the cleanest rule in travel: your bag, your responsibility.

If your checked bag arrives without the original tag, with a damaged tag, with a rush tag, or through a different baggage process than expected, do not just shrug and leave the airport.

It has been revealed that do not rely on a quick conversation at the counter. Conversations disappear the second you walk away. Written reports create a record.

This matters if your bag was mishandled, delayed, retagged, or separated from its original tag.

When your suitcase comes out at baggage claim, do not grab it on autopilot and leave.

Check that it is actually yours. Look at the tag, compare the bag number against your receipt, check your tracker, inspect the condition, and make sure the contents have not obviously been disturbed.

It has been revealed that we have seen people accidentally walk away with someone else’s luggage. It happens more easily than people think, especially after long-haul flights when everyone is tired and half the carousel is filled with identical black suitcases.

Before you leave the airport or customs area, take one minute to confirm everything looks right.

Not necessarily. We have traveled for decades, and carry-on only is not always realistic. Sometimes you need to check a bag, especially on longer trips, family trips, cruises, cold-weather destinations, camera-heavy travel, or extended international travel.

For a smoother trip overall, our easy air travel tips can help before you even reach baggage claim.

For longer flights, our long-haul flight tips can also help make the journey easier before you even get to baggage claim.

The point is not to scare people out of checking luggage. The point is to enhancement your habits.

The old way of checking luggage was simple: check the bag, keep the receipt somewhere, and hope for the best.

It sounds like a lot, but it takes less than two minutes — and those two minutes could make a huge difference if your name ever gets attached to a suitcase that is not yours.

If authorities ever question you about a suitcase that you do not recognize, stay calm.

Do not guess, don’t joke and do not become argumentative.

Ask for legal assistance and show the documentation you collected: your suitcase video, scale photo, baggage tag photo, receipt, tracker information, and photos of what you packed.

This article is not legal advice, but from a traveler’s perspective, the goal is simple: create proof before there is a problem.

If your name is ever attached to a bag you did not pack, your documentation may help show what your real suitcase looked like, what it weighed, what was inside it, and where it went.

Before every checked bag disappears behind the counter, take two minutes to create a simple record of your suitcase.

It has been revealed that that’s it. Two minutes. No drama. No paranoia. Just smart travel.

Recent findings suggest that most airport workers are honest, and most checked bags arrive without a problem. But airport systems are massive, complicated, and not completely invisible-proof. Once your bag disappears behind the counter, you are trusting a chain of people, machines, tags, scans, and systems to keep your suitcase connected to your name.

That is usually fine — until it is not.

So before your next flight, take two minutes to protect yourself. Film your bag. Photograph your tag. Keep your receipt. Use a tracker. And never carry anything for anyone else.

In a recent development, the goal is not to travel scared. The goal is to travel smarter.

Because when travelers get smarter, scams get riskier for the people trying to pull them off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Jonquel Jones picks up the phone to chat with us at Condé Nast Traveler, she’s in the back of her team bus, having just arrived in Minneapolis with the New York Liberty. In two days, she and her teammates will make WNBA history, defeating the Minnesota Lynx in Game 1 of the 2026 Playoffs. Their win will be the first time a No. 8 seed—the lowest-ranked team to qualify for the playoffs—beats a No. 1 seed, the league’s top-ranked team. But for Jones, such a victory will hardly qualify as new territory.

The 32-year-old Upcoming York Liberty center has spent the better part of the last decade breaking records: She has taken home all four major MVP honors, became the first international player named All-Star MVP, and helped lead the Liberty to their first-ever championship in 2024.

According to recent reports, an athletic career like hers means rarely staying in one place for long—a reality reflected in the setting of our conversation. Between WNBA seasons and stints playing overseas, Jones has built a life where traveling has become a part of the game (off the court, of course). But no matter how far basketball takes her, there’s one destination that brings her back to herself: her home country, the Bahamas.

When her schedule finally allows for a pause, returning to the islands offers Jones a different kind of home-court advantage—and a chance to reconnect with the places and people that matter most to her. We caught up with the WNBA All-Star to talk through a typical trip back to the Bahamas, from the comforts she packs before leaving Newly introduced York City and her in-flight essentials to the Bahamian delicacy she never returns without—plus how to make it yourself!

What trip are you unpacking for us?A trip to Grand Bahama, where I grew up.

Tell us about the itinerary: Where did you stay? What were the highlights?I always stay at my condo, which is close to where my family lives. I have homes both in the Bahamas and in New York. My grandmother, parents, cousins, nieces, and nephews are all still on the island. Aside from two of my siblings, pretty much my entire family still lives in the Bahamas, so getting to spend time with them is really special.

It has been revealed that how often do you visit?I try to go back whenever I can, but it all depends on my schedule. This year’s off-season gives me a few months off, so I’ll be spending at least two months back home. During the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, though, I was only able to go for seven days. It really varies from year to year.

Sources indicate that who were you traveling with?I always bring my dog Rylo with me when I go back home. He’s a seven-year-old poodle mix, and he loves the Bahamas. I got him in 2019, right before COVID. I grew up around a lot of dogs—mostly yard dogs—and I’ve always had a special connection with animals.

Growing up, I had a dog named Princess, and she was my dog, for real—no pun intended. She went everywhere with me. Whether I was riding over to my grandmother’s house, walking to the beach, or playing basketball, she was always right there. She’d sit on the sidelines and watch me play, making sure I was okay. Princess was my first experience with unconditional love, and she’s the reason I fell in love with dogs.

Sources indicate that on this trip, did you overpack, underpack, or get it just right?I’m definitely an overpacker. I like bringing little comforts from home in New York, like my favorite matcha and coffee beans. I’m a big matcha fan, so I’ll even bring my entire matcha set. There’s a Japanese market called Midoriya Japanese Grocery on Fifth Avenue in Brooklyn that has amazing matcha, and I always stock up before a trip. I’m also a big fan of Stumptown Coffee; Hair Bender is my go-to blend. It’s nice to have a few pieces of my everyday routine with me. They help me settle in.

Sources indicate that what drugstore essentials do you always have in your backpack?Claritin! I have to have it with me. I have terrible allergies, and something about the pine trees in the Bahamas make them go crazy. I actually recently brought a friend back home with me, and the two of us spent the entire trip passing the bottle back and forth. Without my Claritin, it definitely takes me longer to acclimate.

Sources indicate that what is a little luxury you always bring with you?A nighttime face mask. I love having something I can use to pamper myself during a little girls’ night in. A good overnight mask is my go-to when I want to firm up my skin or wake up with a little extra glow.

Recent findings suggest that do you have a favorite item of travel clothing to fly in?Comfort is definitely my priority when I travel. I'm not just looking after myself, but Rylo, too, so I want to make sure we're both comfortable. Dogs can pick up on nervous energy, and I don't want him to sense that from me. I try to stay in a relaxed, zen state so we can both enjoy the trip.I'm a Nike athlete, and I love their top and bottom sets. They have great two-piece options that are simple but fashionable, which makes them perfect for traveling.

Industry observers note that what's one piece of home you always pack?I’m probably going to sound crazy, but I’m a gamer, and bringing my PlayStation 5 console is a big part of how I get comfortable and settle in when I get back to the Bahamas. I have a whole gaming setup waiting for me at my condo, so all I have to do is plug in my PS5 and I’m ready to go. It’s one item I never travel home without.

Recent findings suggest that what's your go-to snack to keep on hand for long travel days?It’s probably not the healthiest choice, but I grew up eating Cadbury Crunchie Bars. I loved them as a kid, then went through a phase where I stopped eating them. For some reason, though, I’ve recently fallen back in love with them, and they’ve become my go-to. Now they also make Cadbury Crunchie Rocks, which are bite-size, cluster versions of the bar that come in a resealable bag, making them a little easier to travel with. I also love Cadbury Dairy Milk Fruit & Nut. Oh my god, that bar? So good. I feel a little like a granny saying this, but it’s one of my favorites. It has almonds, raisins, and dried fruit—it's delicious. My mom used to buy it when I was growing up, and as a kid, I couldn't understand why she liked it so much. But, lo and behold, I get it now.

According to recent reports, what's your in-flight routine like?I’d say either my Steam Deck, a portable gaming system, or a good book. I’m a big reader and use it to escape. I especially love fiction and fantasy. I recently read The Sword of Kaigen: A Theonite War Story, which has a similar feel to Avatar: The Last Airbender. It’s such a great book, but fair warning: the fight scenes are brutal, so prepare yourself. It’s worth it, though.I also can’t travel without my Bose headphones. Those are an absolute must.

What's a fragrance that never leave home without?I love, love, love the LV Lovers fragrance by Pharrell Williams in collaboration with Louis Vuitton.

Recent findings suggest that last question: What souvenirs do you bring home?Whenever I leave the Bahamas, I always bring back conch. It’s a Bahamian delicacy that you’ll find in every dish, and can be prepared in so many different ways. My favorite is conch fritters, made by tenderizing the conch and mixing it into a batter with onions, thyme, and celery.I always bring back bags of frozen conch fritter batter so I can enjoy a taste of home once I'm back in the United States. Whenever I'm craving them, I just thaw the batter, add a little baking powder, and deep-fry it. And just like that, I have fresh conch fritters. The closest comparison I can make is a hush puppy. If you can't find conch, you could probably try making them with calamari, too.

Brazilian Court Orders Arrest of the Buenavista Over Corazul Dispute

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (403 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cruiseindustrynews

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A Brazilian court ordered the arrest of Corazul’s the Buenavista at the Port of Santos after the cruise line’s exclusive Brazilian distributor claimed it was owed about $270,000 (R$1.48 million), according to a court decision dated Nov.
  • Judge Frederico dos Santos Messias of the São Paulo State Court of Justice’s specialized maritime court granted the request from R11 Travel Viagens e Turismo against GLCL Global Cruiseline Ltd., the Cyprus-registered company that operates as Corazul.
  • The judge issued the order without first hearing from Corazul, the decision showed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A Brazilian court ordered the arrest of Corazul’s the Buenavista at the Port of Santos after the cruise line’s exclusive Brazilian distributor claimed it was owed about $270,000 (R$1.48 million), according to a court decision dated Nov. 13.

Judge Frederico dos Santos Messias of the São Paulo State Court of Justice’s specialized maritime court granted the request from R11 Travel Viagens e Turismo against GLCL Global Cruiseline Ltd., the Cyprus-registered company that operates as Corazul.

The judge issued the order without first hearing from Corazul, the decision showed.

It has been revealed that the order barred the Buenavista from leaving Brazilian waters. The court said the ship was anchored off Santos for repairs.

The judge set security at about $323,000 (R$1.78 million) and said the ship would be released if Corazul deposited that amount or posted a bank guarantee.

It has been revealed that according to the decision, R11 said Corazul owed about $1.27 million (R$6.96 million) under a four-year exclusive distribution agreement signed in March. That figure included about $780,000 (EUR 675,000) in unpaid quarterly marketing contributions. After subtracting about $1 million (R$5.48 million) in passenger funds it held, R11 put the net balance at about $270,000.

Industry observers note that the filing, as summarized by the court, described a series of disruptions including the cancellation of the Buenavista’s European season in June; the cancellation of its Oct. 23 inaugural Brazilian cruise nine days before departure and complaints about onboard service on the Oct. 30 sailing. The tech giant has since suspended operations and R11 has stopped selling cruises on the ship.

According to recent reports, R11 stated Corazul demanded $400,000 on Nov. 4 before it would operate the Nov. 6 departure. R11 refused.

Recent findings suggest that the court noted that only two of the 11 sailings scheduled between Oct. 23 and Nov. 27 operated. Corazul also suspended operations until Nov. 30 and moved the end of its Brazil season up to March 5, 2027. The judge wrote that Corazul’s own communications showed a “serious liquidity collapse.”.

According to recent reports, the dispute is headed to arbitration in São Paulo under AMCHAM, the American Chamber of Commerce for Brazil. The decision stated that R11 must file within 30 days or the order lapses. Corazul has five days after being served to contest it.
